title: Scaling by metric, by schedule and by prediction

videos.script: A group that keeps three instances is safe. It is also wrong for most of the day. {{count}} At three in the morning, three is too many. At noon on a Monday, it is too few. This lesson is about who moves the number. {{thermostat}} The first answer is a thermostat. You tell the group to keep its average CPU at fifty percent. AWS does the arithmetic and writes the alarms. {{steps}} The second answer is a table you write yourself. This far over the line, add this many instances. {{clock}} The third ignores the load and reads the clock. Half past seven in São Paulo, six instances. And the clock is in UTC, unless you say otherwise. {{forecast}} The fourth reads last week and guesses tomorrow. {{lab}} moto stores every one of these policies, and runs almost none of them. It keeps no metrics, so no alarm ever fires on its own. The lesson shows what moto does keep, and says plainly where the rest is AWS's documented behaviour. {{warmup}} And under all four sits the same problem. A new instance takes minutes to be useful, and every policy has to wait for it.
